description: The provided image is a donut chart from the paper “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs,” visually comparing two levels of ambiguity — “Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)” — in terms of deception outcomes: “Deceived,” “Partially,” and “Not Deceived.” The outer ring (Ambiguity 1) is segmented into three colored portions: a large red segment labeled 67.6% for “Deceived,” a yellow segment at 23.5% for “Partially,” and a green segment at 8.8% for “Not Deceived.” The inner ring (Ambiguity 2) mirrors this structure with corresponding colors: red (57.9% “Deceived”), yellow (23.5% “Partially”), and green (10.5% “Not Deceived”). A legend on the right clarifies that red corresponds to “Deceived,” yellow to “Partially,” and green to “Not Deceived,” with identical color coding for both ambiguity levels. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of the “Deceived” category in both ambiguity conditions, with a slight decrease in deception rate from Ambiguity 1 to Ambiguity 2, accompanied by a small increase in “Not Deceived” responses. Percentages are displayed directly on the chart segments, and the inner ring is slightly offset from the outer ring for visual distinction.
